sections.h2: Who bills property tax in Boca Raton?
sections.html:
The Palm Beach County Tax Collector sends one bill, and the Palm Beach County Property Appraiser sets the value. The City of Boca Raton levies only part of it.

The city's August 2026 Property Taxes Explained brochure says a Boca Raton bill carries eight taxing authorities and that only 21.67 percent of the tax goes to the city. The Tax Collector's page says it mails more than 600,000 bills by November 1 to the address on file with the Property Appraiser, and that taxes are payable November 1 through March 31.

  • Value, exemptions and mailing address: Palm Beach County Property Appraiser, (561) 355-2866.
  • Bills, delinquent tax, installment plan, deferral, tax certificates: Palm Beach County Tax Collector, delinquent line (561) 355-2264.
  • City levy and fire assessment: City of Boca Raton, 201 West Palmetto Park Road.

sections.h2: Which taxing authorities appear on a Boca Raton bill?
sections.html:
The city brochure lists eight: the Palm Beach County School Board, Palm Beach County operating and debt, Boca Raton operating and debt, the Health Care District, the Greater Boca Raton Beach and Park District, the Children's Services Council, the South Florida Water Management District and the Florida Inland Navigational District.

The brochure prints a total millage of 16.9090 for its sample, labeled with the 2026-27 column and published during the proposed-rate stage. Confirm the adopted rate for your own parcel on the Property Appraiser's tax roll tools, since taxing districts inside the city differ by location.

sections.h2: What has the Boca Raton city rate done over time?
sections.html:
The city's rate history chart shows the operating rate near 3.45 mills in 2018 and 3.6476 mills for both 2026 and 2027, while a separate debt service rate fell from 0.2245 to 0.0163 over the same span.

Combined, the city's total millage moved only between 3.6788 and 3.6639 across the ten years charted. The brochure's 2027 column is the city's proposed figure, so it reads as a plan, not a final bill. For a seller, that means the city's own slice is steady and the larger swings come from the school board and county lines.

The brochure also compares Boca Raton's fire assessment, which it prints at $170.00, with other South Florida cities, and says unincorporated Palm Beach County pays a fire MSTU based on assessed value instead. Fire assessments are non-ad valorem, so they sit on the bill beside the millage.

sections.h2: When are Boca Raton property taxes due?
sections.html:
Pay between November and March. Taxes turn delinquent in April, and there is no discount in March.

The Palm Beach County Tax Collector prints the early payment ladder: 4 percent in November, 3 percent in December, 2 percent in January, 1 percent in February, no discount in March and delinquency in April. Gross tax is due March 31. A date that falls on a weekend or holiday moves to the next business day.

Once delinquent, the tax cannot be paid online, and the postmark is no longer proof of payment. Payments must arrive by the last working day of the month to count for that month. Delinquent balances can be confirmed through the Tax Collector's delinquent line.

sections.h2: How do exemptions and caps work for Boca Raton homes?
sections.html:
File your homestead application with the Palm Beach County Property Appraiser by March 1, with the home your permanent residence on January 1.

The city brochure's sample shows the structure: a $50,000 homestead exemption against most levies and $25,000 against school district tax, matching the state rule that the second $25,000 does not apply to school taxes. The brochure's footnote says Amendment 1 gave a double homestead exemption for all levies except school.

  • Save Our Homes limits yearly assessed value growth to the lower of 3 percent or CPI. Florida's chart prints a 2.7 percent cap for 2026.
  • Portability can carry the benefit to a new homestead within three years.
  • A sale resets the property to just value the next January 1.
  • Seniors, disabled veterans and deployed servicemembers have separate exemptions through state law and local ordinance.

sections.h2: What does Boca Raton look like for a seller?
sections.html:
The Census Bureau estimates 101,582 residents in July 2025 in a city of about 29 square miles of land, with a 2020 to 2024 owner-occupied rate of 65.7 percent and a median owner-occupied value of $722,700.

Median gross rent is $2,508 and median household income is $106,273. Some 24.6 percent of residents are 65 or older, so many sellers are retirees downsizing or heirs handling an estate. The city says it has 49,050 dwelling units and an assessed value of $42.7 billion.

At those values, tax effects at closing are large. Florida's documentary stamp tax on a deed is 70 cents per $100 of consideration in all counties but Miami-Dade, and all parties to the deed are liable. Ask the title company to split the current year's tax and any fire assessment on the closing statement.

sections.h2: What if a Boca Raton owner falls behind on tax?
sections.html:
Contact the Tax Collector before the April delinquency date. The Tax Collector lists an installment plan and a homestead tax deferral among its resources.

State rules put deferral applications at March 31 with Form DR-570, and installment applications at May 1 of the assessment year. Tax certificates are sold by June 1, a holder may apply for a tax deed after two years, and on homestead property the opening deed bid includes half the assessed value.

A house with a certificate can still be sold, and the payoff is made from proceeds at closing. Get the written payoff from the Tax Collector, since delinquent amounts change monthly.

faqs.q: Does the City of Boca Raton send its own tax bill?
faqs.a: No. The Palm Beach County Tax Collector sends one bill that includes the city and seven other taxing authorities, per the city's brochure.

faqs.q: What is the Boca Raton millage rate?
faqs.a: It depends on the location. The city's brochure prints 3.6639 mills for the city operating and debt levy and a sample total of 16.9090, labeled as the 2026-27 proposed figure. Check your parcel's adopted rate with the Property Appraiser.

faqs.q: When do Boca Raton property taxes become delinquent?
faqs.a: April 1. Gross tax is due March 31, and delinquent tax cannot be paid online.

faqs.q: Who do I call about my Boca Raton exemption?
faqs.a: The Palm Beach County Property Appraiser at (561) 355-2866. Applications are due March 1.

faqs.q: Does the buyer inherit my Save Our Homes cap?
faqs.a: No. A change of ownership resets assessed value to just value the following January 1, with limited exceptions such as certain spousal transfers.
